content:
Former Liberal minister Philip Ruddock has been appointed to review whether Australian law sufficiently protects the human right to religious freedom, with a report due by 31 March.***

The cabinet-announced review is intended to ease a potentially contentious debate over proposed religious amendments to a same-sex marriage bill, though Treasurer Scott Morrison said the review is “no substitute” for those amendments.***

Prime Minister Malcolm Turnbull said the government needed to examine religious freedom carefully in the context of the “yes” vote and forthcoming marriage equality legislation.***

Senior conservatives have differed on timing: some, including Peter Dutton and Mathias Cormann, suggest a religious freedom bill could be considered next year separately, while Morrison and Liberal senator David Fawcett argue it should be addressed alongside the marriage bill.***

Turnbull cautioned that broader religious freedom reforms could have unintended consequences, particularly if framed as broadly worded, bill-of-rights-style declarations, and said Ruddock—given his experience as Australia’s special envoy for human rights—was well suited to conduct the review.
